title: NetoVIR: a reproducible protocol for virome analysis
protocol: Weigh the faecal material (∼50 mg) and add 500 μL of sterile PBS to attain a 10% (m/v) suspension.
Set the MINILYS homogeniser for 3000 rpm (speed 1) for 60 seconds using 2 mL tubes with O-ring caps.
Centrifuge at 17000g for 3 min. Retrieve at least 150 μL of the supernatant for the next step.
Filter the supernatant obtained in a 0.8 μm (PES) filter at 17000g for 1 min.
Set a heating block for 37°C.
Add 7 μL of 20x homemade buffer (1M Tris, 100 mM CaCl₂ and 30 mM MgCL₂, pH=8) to 130 μL of sample filtrate.
Add 2 μL of benzonase and 1 μL of micrococcal nuclease.
Mix by gently inverting the tubes 3 times.
Incubate for 2h at 37°C.
Stop the reaction by adding 7 μL of 10 nM EDTA.
Freeze samples at –80°C for 24 hours.
Mix in an RNAse-free 2 mL tube: 560 μL AVL buffer and 140 μL sample after nuclease treatment.
Mix the mixture by pulse vortexing.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Change gloves.
Briefly centrifuge the mixture with a microcentrifuge.
Add 560 μL of absolute ethanol to the sample mixture.
Mix very well by pulse-vortex.
Briefly centrifuge the mixture with a microcentrifuge.
Add 630 μL of the sample mixture to the spin column.
Centrifuge at 6000_g for 1 minute, change the collection tube and repeat steps 18 and 19.
Add to the spin column: 500 μL AW1 buffer.
Centrifuge at 6000_g for 1 minute, change the collection tube.
Prepare the AW2 buffer as a concentrate.
Add 500 μl of AW2 buffer to the spin column.
Centrifuge at 20,000 g for 3 min and change the collection tube.
Centrifuge at 20,000 g for 1 min.
Place the spin column in an RNAse-free 1.5 ml tube.
Add 60 μl of AVE buffer to the spin column and incubate for 1 minute.
Pipette the AVE buffer directly onto the filter membrane without touching it with the pipet tip.
Centrifuge at 6,000 g for 1 min.
Store viral RNA and DNA at -80°C.
Mix 0.5 μl of Library Synthesis Solution with 2.82 μl of extracted viral sample by pipetting and incubate in a thermocycler programmed for 95°C for 2 minutes then cool down to 18°C.
To the cooled-primed DNA and RNA (18°C) sample, immediately add 0.78 μl RNAse free water.
Add 0.5 μl Library Synthesis Buffer to the cooled-primed DNA and RNA sample.
Add 0.4 μl Library Synthesis Enzyme to the cooled-primed DNA and RNA sample.
Mix and incubate in a thermocycler programmed for 18°C for 10 minutes.
Incubate at 25°C for 10 minutes.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Incubate at 42°C for 10 minutes.
Incubate at 70°C for 20 minutes.
Store at 4°C.
Add 7.5 μL Amplification mix to the DNA library sample.
Add 60.2 μL RNAse free water to the mixture.
Add 1.5 μL WTA dNTP mix to the solution.
Add 0.75 μL Amplification enzyme to the mixture.
Mix by pipetting thoroughly.
Incubate at 94°C for 2 minutes.
Incubate at 94°C for 30 seconds.
Incubate at 70°C for 5 minutes.
Repeat steps 10 through 12 a total of 17 times.
Purify the PCR product using a standard PCR purification kit.
Add 500 μL binding buffer to the WTA2 amplification product mixture.
Place the spin filter in a 2 mL receiver tube.
Centrifuge at 11000g for 3 minutes.
Place the spin filter in a 1.5 mL receiver tube.
Elute with 50 μL elution buffer.
Incubate for 1 minute.
Centrifuge at 11000g for 1 minute.
Store amplified DNA at -80°C.
Measure the concentration of each WTA2 purified product using Qubit dsDNA HS assay kit.
Set up 0.5 mL Qubit tubes for the standards and samples as required.
Prepare a working solution by adding 199 μL of Qubit dsDNA HS Buffer and 1 μL of Qubit dsDNA HS Reagent per sample.
Load 190 μL of the working solution in standard tubes and 199 μL in sample tubes.
Add 10 μL of standard to respective tubes and 1 μL of sample to each sample tube.
Mix by pulse-vortexing.
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Press dsDNA High Sensitivity as the assay type on the Home Screen of the Qubit Fluorometer and run a new calibration.
Read standard #1 concentration.
Read standard #2 concentration.
Read samples concentration.
Calculate sample concentration according to the manual.
Mix the following in 200 μl PCR tubes: 5 μL Tagment Buffer, 2.5 μL Amplicon tagment mix, and 2.5 μL Amplified DNA (1.2 ng/μl) for DNA tagmentation.
Centrifuge at 280g for 1 min.
Incubate in a thermocycler for 4 min at 55°C followed by cooling to 10°C.
Add 2.5 μL Neutralize Tagment Buffer to the 10 μl of tagmented DNA.
Centrifuge at 280g for 1 min.
To the tagmented DNA (12.5 μl), add 2.5 μL Primer 1 (i7, N70X) and 2.5 μL Primer 2 (i5, S50X).
Add 7.5 μL Nextera PCR master mix to the tagmented DNA mixture.
Centrifuge samples at 280 g for 1 minute.
Incubate in a thermocycler: 95°C for 30 seconds, then 95°C for 10 seconds, followed by 55°C for 30 seconds and 72°C for 45 seconds. Repeat this cycle 15 times.
After the cycles, incubate at 72°C for 3 minutes and then cool to 4°C.
Store amplified DNA at 4°C for a maximum of 24 hours or proceed with PCR clean-up.
Prepare fresh 80% ethanol and vortex AMPure beads for a few seconds.
Mix 25 μL PCR product with 15 μL AMPure beads by pipetting until homogeneous.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Place the plate in the magnetic stand for 2 minutes.
Very carefully remove and discard supernatants.
Keeping the plate on the magnetic stand, add 200 μl of 80% ethanol to each sample.
Incubate the plate/tube at room temperature for ≥ 30 seconds.
Carefully remove and discard the ethanol. Repeat this step once.
Try to remove all residual ethanol by pipetting. Incubate at room temperature for about 3 minutes without drying the beads.
Thoroughly resuspend the beads in 26.25 μl of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) by pipetting them up and down approximately 10 times.
Incubate the plate at room temperature for 2 minutes to elute DNA from the beads.
Place the plate on the magnetic stand for 2 minutes.
Transfer 25 μl of supernatant to new RNAse-free tubes.
Store amplified DNA at -80°C.
Measure the concentration of each library by Qubit as described from step 42 to 51.
Check the size distribution on an Agilent high-sensitivity chip (Bioanalyzer).
Remove reagents from the fridge (4°C) and allow them to reach room temperature for around 30 minutes before use.
Set up the chip priming station’s lever to the lowest position.
Adjust the IKA vortex mixer to 2400 rpm.
Start the software, select assays: High Sensitivity DNA assay.
Name your sample wells on the software.
Prepare the gel-dye mix by adding 15 μL of dye (blue-capped tube) to the red-capped tube.
Vortex the dye mixture and transfer it to a spin filter.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 2240g and discard the filter.
Pipette 9 μL of gel-dye mix in well at the bottom of the well to prevent air bubbles.
Place the chip in the priming station, lock it (click sound).
Position the syringe on 1 mL, set the timer for 1 min.
Press the plunger of the syringe down until it is held by the clip and time it.
Release the clip after 1 minute and ensure it moves up to 0.3 mL.
Pull the plunger back to the 1 mL position.
Add 9 μL of gel-dye mix in the remaining G wells at the priming station.
Load 5 μL of marker (green-capped tube) in all sample wells and ladder well.
Pipette 1 μL of ladder (yellow-capped tube) in the ladder well.
Pipette 1 μL of sample into each of the 11 sample wells.
Vortex the chip for 1 minute using the IKA vortex mixer.
Start the run within 5 minutes after vortexing.
Place the chip carefully in the Bioanalyzer and close its lid.
Check that the dsDNA, High sensitivity DNA option is selected and the names of the samples are correctly filled in.
Start the run; a full run takes around 40 minutes.
Thaw all reagents from the kit: Master mix + Primer premix, ROX, and standards.
Prepare 1:1000 and 1:2000 dilutions of the libraries in 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0.
If the kit is used for the first time, add 1 mL of 10X Primer Premix to 5 mL of 2X KAPA SYBR® FAST qPCR Master Mix and mix.
Add appropriate ROX (High or Low) depending on the qPCR instrument in your lab (0.2 mL).
Prepare master mix accordingly for samples, six standards, and appropriate replicates: 12.4 μL 2x qPCR Master Mix + 10x Primer premix + 50x ROX + 3.6 μL RNAse free-water.
Pipette 16 μL of the mix into each qPCR well.
Add 4 μL of standard or sample, accordingly.
Perform your qPCR with the following cycling conditions: 95°C for 5 minutes, 95°C for 30 s, and 60°C for 45 s (repeat for 35 cycles).
OPTIONAL: Perform a melting curve analysis from 65-95°C.
Dilute the libraries aiming for a 4 nM solution using the concentration obtained for the qPCR and the average size from the Bioanalyzer.
Make a pool taking into account the number of reads desired per sample.
Do not mix on the same pool samples with the same double indexing.
